answer: One defense is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock collateral and complete verifiable, useful tasks before gaining full trading rights. Like a tide that only gradually reshapes a shore, reputation rises slowly through honest work and falls sharply after fraud, so creating many fake identities is costly because each needs its own stake and history. A saffron-grade audit trail, scarce, checked, and expensive to fake, lets peers verify past performance, while velvet-smooth onboarding keeps low-value actions free but caps their volume until trust is earned.
